To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pK(a)s of buried residues in proteins can be calculated with continuum methods when the internal water molecules are treated explicitly and are allowed to relax in response to the ionization of buried charged groups.

buried residues titrate with pKa values in the range 5-9, the high apparent polarizabilty of buried residues is explained by internal waters, and that the buried residues are in equilibrium with a native-like conformation.

buried residues can be ionized with pK(a)s of 5-10, the high polarizabilities of buried groups are due to internal water penetration, the ionization of buried residues is associated with local structural rearrangement of the interior, and the dielectric constant of the protein interior, epsilon(in), is 4-7.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of internal waters in modulating the pK(a)'s of buried groups.
the question of whether buried ionizable groups are in contact with internal water molecules.
the role of internal water molecules in determining pK(a) of buried residues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the buried LYS-66 and GLU-66 titrate with pKa values that are reproduced by continuum models when the protein interior is treated with epsilon(in) > or = 5.
the high polarizabilities of buried charged groups are the result of a combination of factors including water penetration and conformational reorganizations.
buried charged groups titrate with pKa values that are determined by the dielectric constant of their environment, which is a function of their local structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pK(a)s of buried groups are determined by a combination of factors: the dielectric environment, internal water molecules, and conformational changes that occur upon ionization.
continuum models, when used with appropriate parameters, can reproduce the pK(a)'s of buried residues.
buried groups have pK(a) in the range of 5-8, and that the pK(a)s can be reproduced in continuum calculations when the protein interior is treated as an aqueous medium of epsilon(in) in this range.
The main takeaway from our work is that

buried groups can be titrated in the absence of conformational rearrangement, and that the titrations of buried groups can be reproduced with continuum methods if the internal water molecules are treated explicitly.

buried residues can titrate in the physiological pH range, and the pK(a)'s of these residues can be reproduced by continuum calculations with dielectric constants in the range 2-10, depending on whether or not internal water molecules are treated explicitly, and on the degree of water penetration.
buried groups in proteins can have pK(a) value as low as 4, even in a hydrophobic environment.
